Posted December 20, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients

Anyone who has been following the polls and initiatives on medical cannabis could not have been too surprised that a new survey shows 72% of middle age (and older) Americans think that adults should be allowed to legally use marijuana for medical purposes if a physician recommends it.

After all, in November, the medical cannabis initiative in conservative Montana passed by a huge margin with 63% of the vote, exceeding the total for Bush/Cheney at 59%.
See
 We Live In Interesting Times. The Elections and the Cannabis Reform Movement. The Problems With Making Democracy Work Against Prohibitionist Propaganda.
and
 California Democrats Discover Democracy, State Democratic Council Endorses Medical Marijuana. Online Poll of Doctors Shows 76% In Favor. If The People Will Lead, The Leaders Will Follow.

Nonetheless, when the wire services reported Saturday that a survey by the American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) once again produced the same results, the phones started ringing at NORML.

The AARP, with its 35 million members who are at least 50 years old, is one of the most powerful lobbies in Washington, and has been closely allied with the Bush Administration. In fact, the AARP played a key roll in getting Bush's Medicare prescription drug coverage through Congress. This support was highly controversial among AARP members, so Bush owes the AARP management political capital to use a phrase recently adopted by the Prez.

William Novelli, the CEO of the AARP, joined the organization in January of 2000 as Associate Executive Director, Public Affairs, i.e a lobbyist. According to the AARP website, Prior to joining AARP, was President of the Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids.

While that would seem unexceptional, Novelli is generally viewed as an anti-smoking fanatic, and as we all should know by now, the proper name for cannabis is actually smokedmarijuana one word and no medicine is smoked.
See
 No Medicine Is Smoked. Okay, But Why Isn't Cannabis Sold Over-the-Counter? New MAPS/NORML Vaporizer Study Undermines Key Part Of Prohibitionist Party Line On Smoked-Marijuana.

(Not surprisingly, Novelli is also presumed to be a prohibitionist, although no one in Washington is allowed to use that term in public.)

Consequently, these results must have been unwelcome in the AARP executive suite, and this poll was actually the second that AARP has done on the subject this year. Perhaps they were hoping that all the previous polls had been mistaken. However, support was even higher in the more recent poll, indicating that the longstanding trend in public opinion continues to move toward supporting medical cannabis.

There was more bad news for them in the geographic breakdown of the results. It was not surprising that support was strongest in the Northeast (79%) and the West (82%) and lowest on in the Midwest (67%) and Southwest (65%), but if there is any surprise, it would be that in the Southern states, where 70% support medical cannabis!
See
 We Are Winning! Almost One Third In DEAland Now Support " Legalization " of Marijuana 40% In The West. In the Face of the Massive Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign and Spin Control in Polling.

What's a prohibitionist to do?

And what is going on here with this leak? It is not uncommon for a story that is about to go to press to be leaked to the media, but it is unusual when a story is leaked more than a month in advance. (The AARP Magazine will not report on the poll until its March-April issue, which doesn't go to press until late in January.)

At the very least, it has the effect of giving the story long legs. As noted earlier this month, the Supreme Court challenge puts the issue on the public agenda.
See
 We Have Already Won A Lot From The Supreme Court Case, Which Is Good Because That Is Probably All That We Are Going To Get. DEA Changes The Rules on Treating Pain.

But the support of the members of this powerful lobby means that the issue must be considered mainstream or nothing would be. Moreover, the ineffectiveness of the prohibitionist party line on the issue was demonstrated by the responses to two other questions. Only a little more than half of respondents believe that cannabis actually has medical value, and 74% think that cannabis is addictive.
See
 Media Alert: Watch for New NIDA Study Claiming Animal Tests Prove Marijuana Is Addictive. Great Marketing of Prohibitionist Propaganda.

In other words, most older Americans think that sick people should be allowed to use cannabis even if it is an addictive placebo!
See
 Study Shows Both Under and Over Use of Anti-Depressants;
The Context For Medical Marijuana Debate

First, it should be noted that older Americans take huge amounts of prescription drugs which can truly be physically addictive, and they know that they often have serious side effects. So even if someone believes that cannabis is a dangerous and addictive drug as a majority of the House of Representatives once proclaimed, well So what?
See
 Bush's New Freedom Initiative: Treatment For Using Cannabis, From The Wonderful Folks Who Brought Us Vioxx, Baycol, Etc. Author of IOM Report Says, " I can't understand why it isn't rescheduled. "
and
 Documenting DEA Lies About Medical Cannabis Ruling: High Court Upholds Marijuana As Dangerous Drug. But the Court Did Nothing of the Sort.
and
 As House Prepares To Impeach Clinton For Lying, It Passes Resolution Saying
That Marijuana Is " Dangerous And Addictive Drug " And Should Not Be Legalized For Medical Use.

Second, it would appear that most people think that if someone is sick and hope that something will make them feel better, they should not be arrested for using it. After all, who knows better, the DEA/FDA, or the patients and their doctors? (The correct answer is John Walters, of course. In fact, that is the correct answer to every question.)
See
 Bush Should Have John Comical Ali Walters Explain The Iraq War, Then The Media Would Never Ask Any Embarrassing Questions. Doctrine Of Drug Czar Infallibility? Blame Canada, Again.

So, what is a poor prohibitionist to do?

Perhaps their best hope lies in organized quackery. An article, Doctors express concern over marijuana use in today's Honolulu Advertiser illustrates the problem in leaving control of access to the plant in the hands of doctors.

Almost 2,000 patients have registered for the state's medical marijuana program since the state Legislature created it four years ago. (It is run by the state Narcotics Enforcement Division.)

Unfortunately, the article is misleading in that it says, (T)he U.S. Supreme Court is weighing whether laws such as Hawai'i's are valid.

No, it is not. The Court is NOT ruling on the validity of the state laws, but on whether the Federal laws are valid.

The article goes on to say, Dr. Inam Rahman, head of the Hawaii Medical Association, said many members of the physicians association are wary of recommending marijuana to their patients precisely because of that conflict between the federal laws that criminalize marijuana use and the state laws that allow its use for certain medical conditions.

Rahman said physicians worry that the federal government can always come after the doctors.

The Hawaiian Medical Association has a terrible record on medical cannabis, and has consistently misinformed its members about the Federal laws. Hawaii is in the 9th Circuit and doctors there were protected by a 9th Circuit restraining order against the Feds taking any action against doctors for recommending medical cannabis even before the Supreme Court refused to review (and thereby upheld) the 9th Circuit on Oct. 14, 2003.

The high court rarely refuses to hear government appeals of lower court decisions, so this was a dramatic slap in the face for the Feds, but apparently the HMA has heard about that.
See
 Bush Administration Argues That Freedom of Speech Applies to Pharmaceutical Company Ads , But Not Conversations Between Doctors and Patients About Medical Cannabis. We Couldn't Make This Up!
and
 Hawaii Quacks Continue to Betray Their Patients Not All of the Victims of Marijuana Prohibition Have Been Arrested. Not All of the Victimizers Are Narks.
and
 Organized Quacks In Hawaii Continue To Support Arresting The Sick and Dying

The article went on to explain, Rahman, who practices internal medicine, said many doctors are reluctant to recommend marijuana over other available pain treatments. He said marijuana that's smoked is harder to monitor than pills and there's always a potential for abuse.

Actually, smoking (or vaporization) makes it easier for both the patient and the doctor to monitor than any medicine that is ingested. That is one reason that patients like to smoke cannabis. The sad fact is that even four years after the state legislature passed the medical cannabis law over their objections the HMA continues to encourage ignorance.

Last week's Feature Article States Should End The Drug War on DrugSense Weekly was by Sheldon Richman, a senior fellow at The Future of Freedom Foundation concludes with the statement, Medical marijuana does not advance liberty. It only empowers doctors. The idea that government should decide whether marijuana is medicine or not and whether doctors should be permitted to give it to sick people ought to be offensive to any self-responsible American.

In My Generation, Pete Townsend wrote, I hope I die before I get old. He will be 60 next May. (I will be 65 next June.) Inasmuch as he probably knows someone who will provide him with medical cannabis, even though he lives in the prohibitionist UK which is even stalling the approval of GW Pharmaceuticals whole cannabis derivative, I hope he will reconsider, because we are winning!.
